moments.name: 14…Nxb5
moments.headline: 14…Nxb5!! A real sacrifice: Black gives up material and the engine still rates it best.
points: Leaves the queen on d8 where it can be taken.
White can take, but after 15.Rxd8 Nxc3+ 16.Bxc3 Rxd8 the engine rates it 0.00.
Takes the bishop on b5.
Protects the rook on e8, which was hanging.
14…Nxb5 threatens …Nxc3+, with mate in 3, and stops Bxe8.
It threatens …Nxc3+, with mate in 3, so White has to spend the next move on it.

why.title: The idea
why.text: 14…Nxb5!! leaves the queen on d8 hanging. Taking it still leaves Black level.

why.title: What Black gives up
why.text: 14…Nxb5 leaves the queen on d8 hanging to the rook on d1. That's the queen on offer.

why.title: What it does instead
why.text: It takes the bishop on b5. Now White can take only one of the two: the knight on b5 or the queen on d8.

why.title: If White takes the queen
why.text: 15.Rxd8 is met by 15…Nxc3+, taking the knight on c3 with check. Then 16…Rxd8 takes the rook on d8, and 17…Nxe4 takes the e4 pawn. Black is two pawns down: Black holds the balance (0.00). This is White's best try.

why.title: If White takes back on b5
why.text: 15.Nxb5 is met by 15…Qxd1+, taking the rook on d1 with check. Then 16…Qxc1# is mate.

moments.name: 15…Nxc3+
moments.headline: 15…Nxc3+! The only good move here: every alternative is clearly worse.
points: Takes the knight on c3.
The next best move, 15…Rxd8, would drop Black's winning chances from 50% to 14% (+4.84).
15…Nxc3+ wins a rook and a pawn.
Takes the knight on c3 and wins a rook and a pawn once the captures settle.
White answers 16.Bxc3, taking back.
After 16.Bxc3 Rxd8 17.Qe1 Nxe4 18.Ba5 Nd2+, Black comes out 6 points of material up (+0.02).

moments.name: 17…Nxe4
moments.headline: 17…Nxe4!! A real sacrifice: Black gives up material and the engine still rates it best.
points: Puts the knight on e4 where it can be taken.
Taking is too dangerous: White's best reply is 18.Ba5 Nd2+ 19.Kb2 Rd5 instead (the engine rates it +0.16).
Takes the pawn on e4.

Takes the e4 pawn and wins a pawn once the captures settle.

why.title: The idea
why.text: 17…Nxe4!! offers the knight on e4. Taking it leads to mate.

why.title: What Black gives up
why.text: 17…Nxe4 puts the knight on e4 where it can be taken by the queen on e1. That's a knight on offer.

why.title: If White takes the knight
why.text: 18.Qxe4 is met by 18…Rd1+. Then 19…Bc1+ gives check, and 20…Ba3# is mate.

why.title: White's best try
why.text: White's best is to leave the knight alone and play 18.Ba5. Black answers 18…Nd2+, and the knight on e4 gets away. Then 19…Rd5 threatens …Rxa5, winning a bishop, and 20…Rxd2 takes the bishop on d2. Black ends up a pawn ahead: Black holds the balance (+0.16).

why.title: Without the sacrifice
why.text: The best move without the sacrifice, 17…Bb7, is clearly weaker (+0.99 against +0.16). White answers 18.Nf3, threatening Bd2, winning a rook for a piece and a pawn. That would leave Black a little worse.
